rubrics.justification: Provides a generally plausible blastocyst assessment with appropriate caveats about static-image limits, but it questions the reported expansion and A-grade features without strong support and may undercall a lab-scored 3AA embryo.
Integrates age, ovarian reserve markers, prior IVF history, semen parameters, and missing endometrial data well, though it overemphasizes the inconsistency of the DOR label and low MII count.

Reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a logical link from embryo quality and age to prognosis; minor issues include tension between calling the case high quality yet visually below robust 3AA.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice, especially favoring single embryo transfer in a young patient and avoiding unnecessary add-ons; minor deviations include speculative discussion of protocol issues from limited data.
Gives clear, practical next steps for transfer management, uterine assessment, luteal support, and future cycle review, with appropriate nuance about when to escalate evaluation.
